description: Payment API returned 502 for all checkout requests minutes after deployment v3.14.
recent_change: Deployment v3.14 changed upstream block in nginx.conf
root_cause: Nginx upstream pointed to old port 8080 after deployment; service now listens on 8443
solution: Reverted nginx.conf upstream to port 8443 and ran nginx -s reload
failed_attempts: Restarting payment pods did not help

description: Users cannot log in; DB connection pool exhausted.
root_cause: Unindexed session_audit query holding connections open
solution: Added index on session_audit(user_id, created_at) and raised pool timeout
failed_attempts: Scaling auth pods made it worse

description: Search pods restarting every few minutes after index refresh.
root_cause: JVM heap larger than container memory limit
solution: Set -Xmx to 75% of container limit and raised memory limit to 6Gi

description: Email queue backing up for 40 minutes.
root_cause: New SMTP secret not updated in worker deployment
solution: Updated Kubernetes secret smtp-creds and rolled workers

description: Checkout site unreachable for some users.
root_cause: Expired intermediate certificate on load balancer
solution: Installed renewed cert chain and enabled expiry alerts 30 days ahead

description: Payment API returned 502 for all checkout requests minutes after deployment v3.14.
recent_change: Deployment v3.14 changed upstream block in nginx.conf
root_cause: nginx upstream block misconfigured to port 8080 instead of the required 8443 after deployment v3.14
solution: : Memory of incident INC-1001 identified the same upstream port misconfiguration and noted that restarting payment pods did not fix the issue; therefore pod restarts were omitted from the recommended actions.

description: Users cannot log in; DB connection pool exhausted.
root_cause: The newly added session‑audit query is unindexed, causing long‑running DB scans that hold connections and exhaust the database connection pool.
solution: Memory of incident INC-1002 showed that an unindexed session_audit query caused identical symptoms and that scaling auth pods worsened the problem. Therefore, we prioritized adding an index and increasing pool limits, and explicitly avoided pod scaling as a remediation step.
